caption: The PN junction at the physics level the Extra pool tests, in three panels. At rest: the P region (acceptor-doped) holds majority holes with a few minority electrons, the N region (donor-doped) holds majority free electrons with a few minority holes, and near the junction the two recombine, leaving a depletion region containing only fixed ions - negative acceptor ions on the P side, positive donor ions on the N side - whose charge opposes further flow. Forward bias (+ to the P side, - to the N side): the battery pushes holes and electrons toward the junction, the depletion region narrows, and current flows as carriers cross and recombine. Reverse bias (- to the P side, + to the N side): the battery pulls majority carriers away from the junction, the depletion region widens, and essentially no current flows (E6A03). The doping facts anchor E6A02 and E6A04: donor impurities add free electrons (N-type), acceptor impurities add holes (P-type).
spoken: Three panels of a PN junction. A legend marks open circles as holes, filled dots as electrons, and boxed minus and plus signs as fixed acceptor and donor ions. Panel one, at rest: a P-type block full of holes and an N-type block full of electrons meet at a shaded depletion region holding only fixed ions, minus on the P side and plus on the N side. Panel two, forward bias: a battery with its plus terminal to the P side pushes holes and electrons toward the junction; the depletion region is narrow and a bold arrow shows current flowing across. Panel three, reverse bias: the battery is flipped, plus to the N side; carriers are pulled away from the junction, the depletion region is wide, and a crossed-out dashed arrow reads essentially no current.
